name: beast
why: Bayesian phylogenetic sampling of evolutionary trees, real science you can run at home on sequence data.

brief.what_it_is: BEAST (Bayesian Evolutionary Analysis Sampling Trees) is a cross-platform Java program for Bayesian analysis of molecular sequences using MCMC. It takes molecular sequence data, plus optional dates and trait data, and produces posterior samples of rooted, time-measured phylogenies and their parameters. It ships with a graphical setup tool, BEAUti, and a suite of companion programs for analysing the results, including loganalyser, logcombiner, treeannotator, and treestat. The homepage says it is for BEAST X v10.x, currently v10.5.0.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents BEAST as a framework for testing evolutionary hypotheses without conditioning on a single tree topology, rather than only as a way to reconstruct phylogenies. It averages over tree space with MCMC so each tree is weighted by its posterior probability.
brief.how_it_works: BEAST runs MCMC over tree space, so each tree is weighted proportional to its posterior probability. It is built for rooted, time-measured phylogenies under strict or relaxed molecular clock models. BEAUti writes the model setup as an XML file, and the beast program runs the sampler on that file. The companion tools then summarise the logs and trees the run produces. BEAST uses the separate BEAGLE library to speed up its core likelihood calculations.
brief.install_notes: The installing page lists separate instructions for Mac, Windows, and Linux, Unix, or Mac command line. BEAST is Java, so the same code runs anywhere Java is installed, and native packages wrap it with a GUI. The latest release is linked from GitHub at beast-dev/beast-mcmc releases. BEAGLE is a separate library that BEAST uses to accelerate calculations, and the site has its own install page for it. I did not fetch the per-platform install pages, so I cannot confirm first-run or configuration steps.
brief.standout: It is the reference tool for time-calibrated Bayesian phylogenetics, and it comes with a full ecosystem of tutorials (phylodynamics, phylogeography, model selection) and companion programs such as Tracer, TempEst, and FigTree. The homepage notes it is a separate project from BEAST2, which is led by the University of Auckland.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage lists v10.5.0 as current, and the installing page lists v10.5.0-beta5 as the latest version and points users to GitHub issues for bug reports. The site has a citation to a 2025 Nature Methods paper. I did not see a release date or a last-commit date, so the exact age of the latest release is unknown.
brief.caveats: The installing page says the latest build is a beta, which it calls suitable for general use but possibly still buggy. The homepage's version line (v10.5.0) and the installing page's (v10.5.0-beta5) differ slightly. BEAST is for rooted, time-measured trees under molecular clock models, so it is a poor fit for unrooted or clock-free analyses. The BEAST2 project is a separate codebase, and this site is only about BEAST X. The homepage asks users to join the beast-users mailing list for announcements.
quotes: BEAST is a cross-platform program for Bayesian analysis of molecular sequences using MCMC.
It is entirely orientated towards rooted, time-measured phylogenies inferred using strict or relaxed molecular clock models.
BEAST uses MCMC to average over tree space, so that each tree is weighted proportional to its posterior probability.
fetch_log: https://beast.community/ : worked. Homepage is mostly navigation; the body has the 'What is BEAST?' text, the citation, and the install links.
https://beast.community/installing : worked. Gives the latest version, the beta note, and links to the per-platform install pages, which I did not follow. I did not fetch the GitHub releases page.

judge.reason: BEAST makes evolutionary tree space explorable through Bayesian MCMC, a distinctive scientific idea backed by a substantial, maintained tool ecosystem.

entry.title: BEAST
entry.tldr: A Bayesian sampler that infers time-measured evolutionary trees from DNA or RNA sequences, used for real research in viral spread and phylogenetics.
entry.deeper_look:
BEAST (Bayesian Evolutionary Analysis Sampling Trees) is a Java program that takes molecular sequences, with optional sampling dates and trait data, and produces posterior samples of rooted, time-measured phylogenies and their parameters. It uses MCMC, a random walk through the space of possible trees and model settings.

The idea underneath is that a single best tree is the wrong thing to ask for. The homepage describes BEAST as a framework for testing evolutionary hypotheses without conditioning on one tree topology. In its words: "BEAST uses MCMC to average over tree space, so that each tree is weighted proportional to its posterior probability." Uncertainty stays in the answer instead of being hidden.

The workflow is a pipeline. BEAUti, a graphical tool, writes the model setup as an XML file. The beast program runs the sampler on that file. Then loganalyser, logcombiner, treeannotator and treestat help you summarise the logs and trees. BEAST also uses the separate BEAGLE library to speed up its likelihood calculations.

It is entirely oriented towards rooted trees under strict or relaxed molecular clock models. Around it sits an ecosystem of tutorials covering phylodynamics, phylogeography and model selection, plus companion programs such as Tracer, TempEst and FigTree. It is a way into Bayesian inference as practised in real science.
entry.install:
brew install beast
Requires Java (the formula pulls in openjdk@25) and the BEAGLE library, both installed as dependencies. You will need sequence data in order to do anything useful; the site's tutorials are the place to find examples.

try_this.what_happens: Lists the command-line options for running the sampler on an XML file.
Opens the graphical tool where you import sequences and set up a model, then save it as the XML file that beast runs.
Shows the options for summarising the sampled trees into a single annotated tree.

entry.whats_unique: It is the reference tool for time-calibrated Bayesian phylogenetics, with a full set of companion programs and tutorials. It is a separate project from BEAST2.
entry.caveats: The installing page calls the latest build a beta, suitable for general use but possibly still buggy, and it only handles rooted, time-measured trees under clock models.
